answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a copper bond before it may vote or claim payments. Random audits compare work histories and communication patterns; identities caught coordinating or copying one another lose their bonds and reputation. New agents must wander through low stakes tasks before gaining influence, while independent agents build trust by solving different problems across the reef. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and risks losing each deposit, making mass identity creation more expensive than its influence.
